placements.why: The database migration from PostgreSQL to QuantumDB is an architecture-level decision about core data infrastructure. No existing strata category holds this; the content calls for an organizational tier for architecture decisions that future envelopes will continue to populate.
placements.title: architecture-level technology decisions
placements.frame: what architecture decisions are being made about core infrastructure, and what drives them?

placements.title: switching database technology for quantified performance and cost gains
placements.frame: how does a database migration decision get driven and justified by measurable performance and cost metrics, and what does the recording of that decision reveal about how it was settled?
placements.why: Dave's decision to switch from PostgreSQL to QuantumDB is driven by 10x query performance and lower licensing cost, performed as settled through present-continuous ratification ('we're switching'), then recorded as a bullet under 'Key decisions' with a Q3 2026 timeline. This is a thematic subject — technology migration for quantified benefits — that future envelopes could continue feeding. src-4 (performance gain) and src-5 (timeline) are position-grain evidence supporting this leaf, not leaves themselves.
